# SPD-040 — Bash hook: a read-write redirection <> opens its target for writing but is skipped as input

## Brief
IN_REDIRECTS holds <>, so separate_redirects drops its operand unchecked; <> opens the file O_RDWR, and 1<>file lets the command overwrite it from the start without truncation. A member can write any protected file (Laws 1 and 5) silently. Found in SPD-039 probing; outside its brief (zsh glob operators).

Evidence: Probe zsh 5.9 -f and -o nobareglobqual in a scratchpad: echo x 1<>ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md over a file holding orig left x then ig, the file changed. analyse_command on that line records no redirect (redirects []), so bash_reason checks nothing. bash 3.2 supports n<> the same way. Fix sketch: treat <> (with or without an fd prefix) as an output redirection in separate_redirects, keeping its operand as a target.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, no children: a narrow parser fix in separate_redirects (<> and n<> as write redirections keeping their operand as a target) with red-first tests and zsh/bash probes. Branch waits for SPD-041's merge, since SPD-041 rewrites the same function (Eric's call, 2026-09-14).

## Outcome
The Bash hook reads the read-write redirection <> as a write: it moved to OUT_REDIRECTS and its operand, numeric and dash names included, is always kept as a target, so it goes through the path rule, glob and brace readings, redirect_cwds, the state directory and Law 1. echo x 1<>ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md is now refused for members and Spud. Probed in zsh 5.9, bash 3.2 and sh; ReadWriteRedirectTest, 9 methods, red first; a 2,241-string differential changed only new <> lines. Suite 522 OK on the branch, merged into main. Proposal 38 became SPD-045 (P3).
